conviction_note: One real negative stands out. On 29 Jul management cut its 2026 external cost-pressure estimate to $45-55m from $60-70m, citing easing bunker fuel. Since then Brent closed above $100 on 9 Sep, averaged about $114 in September, and Q4 bunker forecasts were raised by more than $100/mt twice. That puts the cost guide and the $230-240m EBITDA guide at risk. Against it: EPS beats of more than 35% in two of the last three quarters against a thin, disputed bar; an insider purchase; the Del Monte Foods outlook raised and inside guidance; and a stock already down 13% since 9 Sep and 6.65% above its 52-week low. Findings sum to -0.9, impact_scaled is (2*0.45-1)*6.0 = -0.6. Both measurements agree in sign and both are small. The reaction history (+3.8, -6.4, +5.5, -0.2) turns on the cost and guide line rather than on EPS.

Revenue consensus is $1.16-1.173B across the same sources. findings.finding: Oil and bunker fuel spiked after the 29 Jul call, the reverse of the condition that justified the cost-pressure cut. On 29 Jul DMC cut its 2026 external cost-pressure estimate from $60-70m to $45-55m, citing easing bunker fuel, diesel and fertilizer. Brent then closed at $101.21 on 9 Sep, its highest close since 22 May, and averaged about $114/bbl in September. Ship & Bunker raised its Q4 2026 G20 VLSFO forecast to $882/mt from $758/mt, its second raise of more than $100/mt in two months. DMC runs its own refrigerated fleet. The likely outcome is a higher cost-pressure figure and a pressured $230-240m EBITDA guide. September alone falls in Q3, and July-August oil was lower.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (2026-05-05): the company flagged $40-45m of cost pressures and an extra $20-25m of FX/logistics headwinds; the stock closed -6.42%. Q2 2026 (2026-07-29): cost pressures cut and the Del Monte Foods guide raised; +3.79%. The cost/guide line is the one this name has traded on.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock fell from 32.87 on 9 Sep to 28.66, so the oil move has reached the price in part. What the market has not seen is the company's own updated cost-pressure number and whether the EBITDA range holds. The consensus is still split between $0.46 and $0.51, which suggests estimates have not been uniformly refreshed. If the market had fully priced a guide cut, the stock would sit at or below its 52-week low of 26.47 rather than 6.65% above it.
findings.independence: Brent $101.21 close on 9 Sep, the highest since 22 May (ShipUniverse, 2026-09-10, https://www.shipuniverse.com/news/brent-breaks-100-as-bunker-costs-surge-and-2027-outlook-shifts/). The company's own bunker sensitivity comes from the Q2 call summary (https://quartr.com/events/del-monte-corporation-dmc-q2-2026_3PeB6qX5). This is macro-to-company transmission; the company has not yet confirmed it for H2.

findings.finding: Banana segment cost pressure probably persists into Q3. Q2 banana gross margin was 2.3% against 7.3% a year earlier: $8.4m GP on $361.1m sales, with weak North American demand and higher per-unit production, procurement and ocean freight costs. Peer Dole reported on 10 Aug, after DMC last spoke, that Fresh Fruit gross profit fell on higher fruit sourcing costs. Net of the rest: bananas are 30% of sales but only 7% of Q2 gross profit, while Prepared Foods (19% of sales, 37% of GP, 18.9% margin) is growing, so the segment's drag on the total is limited.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: banana GP fell 72% YoY and the stock still rose +3.79% on Del Monte Foods and the guide. Banana weakness has not driven the reaction on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The Q2 banana collapse was public, and the four Costa Rica farm closures came with a $10.6m impairment. What is new is Dole's 10 Aug confirmation that sourcing costs stayed high. If the market expected a banana recovery, the stock would not be 33% off its high.
findings.independence: Dole plc Q2 2026 8-K, 2026-08-10: 'Gross Profit decreased $23.0 million, primarily due to higher cost of sales which were impacted by higher fruit sourcing costs in the Fresh Fruit segment' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001857475/000185747526000074/doleplcreportssecondquarte.htm).

findings.finding: Avocado prices remain lower on oversupply. Mission Produce reported on 8 Sep for May-July 2026: per-unit avocado prices down 9% and volume up 38% on higher Mexican yields. DMC's Q2 already cited lower avocado prices from industry-wide oversupply in Fresh and Value-Added, so Q3 F&VA pricing is likely soft as well.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated reaction to an avocado line. Q2 F&VA sales fell to $569.3m from $649.9m and the stock rose +3.79%.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer's print after DMC last spoke confirms the trend continued through July. DMC already flagged it, so this is largely priced and kept small. Avocados are a minor line within F&VA.
findings.independence: DMC's own Q2 release on lower avocado selling prices from oversupply (https://s21.q4cdn.com/266848147/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Del-Monte-Corporation-Reports-Second-Quarter-Earnings-for-Fiscal-2026-Press-Release-07-29-2026.pdf).

findings.finding: DMC has a pattern of large EPS beats against a thin, disputed consensus. Q2 2026 adjusted EPS was $0.72 against roughly $0.53 (+36%), and Q3 2025 was about $0.69 against $0.50 (+38%, secondary source). Both came with revenue misses: Q2 $1.219B against about $1.30B. The Q3 2026 bar is $0.46 (Benzinga/TipRanks) or $0.51 (ChartMill, 2 analysts). Another EPS beat is more likely than not, but the reaction to these beats was +3.79% and -0.15%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat (+36% EPS, revenue miss): +3.79%. Q3 2025 beat (+38%, revenue miss): -0.15% (34.36 to 34.31, Yahoo bars). The market pays little for EPS beats here.
findings.why_not_priced: With 2-5 analysts and sources $0.05 apart, the bar is not a firm market expectation. A repeat beat would surprise a mechanical consensus. Rule 6 caps this small because the bar is disputed. If the beat were priced, sources would agree on a higher number.
findings.independence: Benzinga consensus page (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DMC/earnings-forecasts) carries the Q2 actual against estimate. Q3 2025 adjusted net income of $33.1m is in the company 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1047340/000104734025000131/october292025-earningspr.htm).

findings.finding: On 29 Jul the Del Monte Foods outlook was raised to $625m sales / $35m adj EBITDA from $600m / $23m, with integration described as 'ahead of expectations'. In Q2, Prepared Foods earned $44.6m GP at an 18.9% margin, 37% of company GP. Its Q3 contribution is inside the raised guide. Upside comes only if integration keeps beating, for example a second raise or synergy upsizing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 Del Monte Foods raise coincided with +3.79%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely inside the guide, so sized near zero. The only unpriced part is a further raise, and nothing found after July points to one.
findings.independence: Q2 press release segment table: Prepared Foods $236.1m sales, $44.6m GP (https://s21.q4cdn.com/266848147/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Del-Monte-Corporation-Reports-Second-Quarter-Earnings-for-Fiscal-2026-Press-Release-07-29-2026.pdf). Same company source as the guide.

findings.finding: The President & COO (Mohammed Abbas) bought 12,000 shares in the open market on 4 Aug at $29.89, about $359k, after the Q2 print. The stock is now below his purchase price at 28.66. The only other insider transaction since then is a PSU tax-withholding sale of 245 shares by an SVP on 8 Sep at $32.03, which is not discretionary.
findings.why_not_priced: A public Form 4, but small, and the stock has since fallen through his price. It signals management's view of value after Q2, not knowledge of Q3.
findings.independence: SVP Form 4, a withholding sale, not a signal (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1047340/000176973726000009/wk-form4_1788988469.xml).

findings.finding: Both 2026 10-Qs (filed 2026-05-06 and 2026-07-31) contain the term 'IEEPA' per EDGAR full-text search. DMC was importer of record for bananas and pineapples from Costa Rica and Guatemala under the 10% reciprocal tariff until tropical fruit was exempted. Refunds via CBP's CAPE tool, launched 20 Apr, are paid within 60-90 days of acceptance. A refund gain could be recognized in Q3, but the amount and whether it was already recognized could not be read.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for DMC. On 2026-09-10 four US names carried tariff-refund theses and split by guidance direction (LESSONS rule 2).
findings.why_not_priced: The amount is not disclosed in anything read. Q3 2025 sales rose on tariff-related price adjustments in North America, so tariffs were passed through and a refund is a below-the-line one-off with no path to the guide. Sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: CBP CAPE timing (https://www.barclaydamon.com/publications/q3-2026getting-your-money-back-where-the-tariff-refund-process-stands-after-the-us-supreme-court-invalidates-tariffs). The DMC amount is unconfirmed.

findings.finding: The Costa Rican colón stayed strong in Q3, around 449-454 per USD in mid-September. Q2 already cited unfavorable colón FX as a gross-profit headwind in both Banana and F&VA, and the 21 Apr Freshplaza report called the appreciation a 20-year high. The headwind continues in Q3 local costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cited in Q1 (FX headwind guide, -6.42%) and in Q2 (+3.79%). It is not separable.
findings.why_not_priced: Known and already guided: FX was half of the $20-25m extra headwind flagged in May. This is a proxy with no company Q3 number, kept small.

findings.finding: $100.2m remained under the buyback at 26 Jun. In Q2 the company bought 465,213 shares at an average of $34.40 ($16.0m). With the stock now at 28.66, 17% below that average, Q3 repurchases are plausible. The $0.30 quarterly dividend is about a 4.2% yield. Debt rose to $414.6m (revolver $413m of $750m) after the Del Monte Foods deal, and Amendment No. 3 (15 Jul) increased revolving commitments, which funds the acquisition.
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 buyback volume is unknown until the release. Small.
findings.independence: 10-Q filed 2026-07-31 on revolver and Amendment No. 3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1047340/000104734026000042/fdp-20260626.htm). Same company as the source.

baseline_tension: The baseline gives no skew, a thin option market and a 20-day run-up of -6.3% with the stock near its 52-week low. The oil/guide negative points the same way as the drawdown, which suggests it is partly priced. The EPS-beat history and insider buy point the other way. Net, the lean is mildly negative and p_up sits at 45, close to 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed): oil/bunker guide finding -2.0 to -1.5
Rule 6 (disputed bar, $0.46 vs $0.51): EPS-beat-history finding capped from +1.0 to +0.6
Rule 6 (inside the guide): Del Monte Foods finding +0.5 to +0.3
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): banana finding -0.5 to -0.4, as Prepared Foods carries 37% of GP
Rule 2 (one-off with no path to the guide): IEEPA finding +0.2 to +0.1
Rule 7: short interest checked at 4.6% of float, not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk; skew is null
Net: the sum is unchanged at -0.9 because the cuts landed on both sides; p_up 45 and abs_move 6.0 are unchanged
